decision.reason: [ev-689bc0108c6c] names the subject (`tls.caOptional`) and the change (removed). But it lumps eight targets into one line: the ForwardAuth middleware plus seven providers (HTTP, Consul, Etcd, Redis, ZooKeeper, Consul Catalog, Docker). Neither it nor the surrounding Deprecated Options Removal section ([ev-4a489b1e9ff3], [ev-dbef3e2e8163], [ev-989a451dfcd4], [ev-d6a3846e479f]) says what happens to a configuration that still sets the option. On top of that, the v3.0.0 Middleware CRD schema [ev-0842f8f3bd9d] still contains spec.forwardAuth.tls.caOptional, which conflicts with the stated removal and leaves open whether the field is rejected or silently ignored. We need evidence of the actual runtime or validation behaviour, and of how each provider's removal shows up, before the consequence can be written.
